# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: COLE OF SPYGLASS MOUNTAIN
Author: Arthur Preston Hankins. Dodd, Mead, 1923.
Dedication: to Maynard Shipley (scientific material).

**Ch I The Slug.** Spring, weedy vacant lot, Hathaway city. Four boys (11-15). Joshua Cole (14; coal-black hair, gray-blue eyes, ascetic Grecian nose) holds chip 4 in. above ground with slug (*Limax Campestris*). Bets: Joshua's brother Lester (11); tow-headed gambler "Towhead" (milky moony agate); black-and-white agate. Slug descends on mucus thread; Joshua refuses to lift chip ("wouldn't be fair"). Tardy for school. Teacher Silvanus Madmallet ("Ole Madhouse", "Ole Hothatchet", "Ole Sorehammer"; tall, long-beaked, "Spare the rod"). Joshua stands up, refuses to sit ("I won't set down"), defends Lester. Lester sent to hall with strap. Joshua grabs iron poker from coal-box.

**Ch II Spawn of the Devil.** Madmallet's feud: Joshua poor at arithmetic/grammar, good at geography, history, composition. Madmallet found Proctor's *Other Worlds Than Ours* hidden; sent note home; father ducked Joshua in tub. Joshua threatens Madmallet with poker ("Don't you hit my brother"); Madmallet backs off; expels Joshua, suspends Lester one week. Boys in vacant lot; Joshua plans to go West. Takes father's razor from father's room. Lies to mother; Zida Hunt (negro cook/maid, friend) says nothing. Slug walks razor edge. Joshua plans to ambush Slinky Dawson (teacher's pet, freckled, milk-blue eyes) carrying note.

**Ch III The Girl at the Crescent.** John Cole: traveling hardware salesman, drinker, gambler, womanizer, brute; hates Joshua, tolerates Lester. Mother Blanche Florence (Florence family came with Lord Calvert to Maryland; she married Cole against family wishes); home 355 Grant Avenue. Father's books-burning list: Steele's *Chemistry*, Darwin's *Origin of Man* and *Descent of Man*, Huxley's *Man's Place in Nature*. Joshua intercepts Slinky; note addressed "Mrs. John H. Cole, Three fifty-five Grant Avenue. Kindness of Albert Dawson"; Joshua tears it up. Joshua famed roller-skater at Crescent Rink (taught opera troupe). Meets red-gold-haired girl with Oriental-topaz eyes, who asks him to help her skate.

**Ch IV The Gypo Queen.** Girl = Madge Mundy (says 11; large for age). Father "Bloodmop" Mundy (fiery red hair, railroad gypo/contractor); mother Elizabeth (black hair, educated). Gypo camp by railroad tracks; Madge drives horses on slip. Joshua says he's 15 (actually lacks nine months). Joshua asks to go West with them. Lester vanished from rink. Joshua tells gang (Spud Mulligan, "Did" Eustace). Spud rings Cole bell; mother says Joshua "can't come out" (locked up).

**Ch V The Gypo Camp.** Joshua sleeps in boxcar; eats sandwiches; switchman directs him to camp. Breakfast with Madge and mother; cook serves granite pans. Bloodmop: "Well, who in the dickens is this?"; "Think ye could skin Jack an' Ned on roller-skates?" (Jack and Ned = mules). Bloodmop kisses wife. Joshua tells Mrs. Mundy of father's duckings. Mrs. Mundy: "Joshua can find something to interest him about camp."

**Ch VI The Wreck of the Good Ship "Argo".** Bloodmop tells wife: Ole Ambrose (former Cole stable man) confirms abuse; Bloodmop says cops are hunting Joshua. Mrs. Mundy: "old head on his shoulders," "stating his business in this world." Bloodmop wants Joshua as cook's helper; hints Madge/Joshua romance; Bloodmop's pride in Florence family. Joshua and Madge under stars: Orion (Belt, Sword, Betelgeuse, Bellatrix, Nebula, Rigel), Sirius, Pointer, Pole Star; Big Dipper; "five hundred centuries"; nearest star 25 million million miles; quotes "Prisoners are we on a rudderless ship" and Jason's *Argo* passage (Golden Fleece). Hand on shoulder: plainclothes detective (piggish eyes) takes razor. "Yer dad wants you."

**Ch VII Joshua Walks With His Father.** Detective Dickinson (big, has kids) took Joshua to Cole house; warned father against ducking. Father: "Go up to your room." Lester confined; telegram recalled father. Next morning: father takes Joshua walking to hardware stores; then police station, sergeant ("Bad actor, is he? Um!"); police court. Police judge (short, fat, fair, blond, big blue eyes): "Incorrigible." Father: poker threat. Father's private threat: "What I have done to you in the past won't be worth considering." Commitment to House of Refuge until age 21 (Joshua: "Yes, sir"). Dickinson's advice: "Don't fight back. Stand for anythin' they hand you."

**Ch VIII Number 5635.** House of Refuge (outskirts; spiked brick fence). Superintendent (tall, white skin, veiny hands): Joshua's grandfather **Peter D. Florence** founded it. Joshua becomes **Number 5635** ("Fifty-six thirty-five"). Outfitted in gray with brass buttons, red stripes, skull cap, brogans; monitors strip and mock him; he doesn't fight back. **Mr. Beaver Clegg**, head of Juvenile Department: ugliest face (twisted nose, uneven eyes, crooked lips), Lincoln-like; eyes turn purple when moved. Variable-star observer, 3-inch refractor on roof; member International Society of Variable Star Observers. Discusses slug's mucilage ("tapioca puddin'"); Algol variables; Joshua: "I'm gonta be a scientist."

**Ch IX Truth and Honor.** Routine: sewing, schoolroom (7-9 pm), bed at 9, story-telling. Clegg takes Joshua up to roof at night to view Moon: Clavius (143 mi.), Tycho (54 mi.), Blancanus (24,000 ft deep); Flammarion's *Astronomy*. Joshua's "Truth and Honor" (T-and-H) medal; framed and tormented by inmates; "tony" nickname. Inmate spat on him: **Number Twenty-three forty-four** (Felix Wolfgang). Joshua challenges: "Kid, I'm goin' to whip you for spittin' in my face."

**Ch X Pardoned.** Fight: Joshua beats 23-44 (gouged, bit thumb). Joshua deliberately lowered his record to avoid parole. Clegg: "At last... I thought you could hold out." Punished in North Wing basement with bamboo rod (same number of stripes as the other boy). Second T-and-H medal; board lets him stay. Mother Blanche dies; Joshua arrives too late. Uncle **Peter Henry Florence** (flabby, querulous, from Virginia) visits, forgets. Clegg dies (heart failure); note reveals Clegg engineered Joshua's roof lessons; bequeaths telescope, books, photographs. Joshua pardoned at 20 ("six years" in House of Refuge). Lester (shoe store, refuses aid, snickers "Tony"). Joshua boards freight; Wolfgang on same train roof.

**Ch XI An Offer of Partnership.** Ride to Pittsburgh; brakeman ejects him. Lecture-telescope in village at moonrise: 10 cents per look; earns 16 dimes and 6 nickels. **The Whimperer** (John Yegg, artificial acid scar, dislocates arm act, whimpermeter sob-poem card; alias "De Whimperer"): offers partnership, "youse'll be me road-kid."

**Ch XII Whimpermeter.** Joshua accepts for Westward passage; poem "A blighted life, a broken soul." "Lump" and "set-down" slang. Campfire in river bottom.

**Ch XIII The Partnership Dissolved.** Whimperer meets **Slim Wolfgang** (Felix Wolfgang; sandy hair, freckled, husky voice; Joshua's road shadow) in woods; Slim pays five bones (Whimperer wanted ten). Slim wants Joshua watched. Freight out at night. Nearly a year of tramp life (sand-houses, jungles, sheep car). Joshua tries to escape, Whimperer tracks him. Whimperer learns telescope value ($500). Joshua wakes: telescope gone; Whimperer had left at a stop.

**Ch XIV Man and the Slug.** Essay on man as human chameleon. Starving near Southern Colorado; sees slug on grass; despairs; re-performs razor-slug on stick; sobs, prays ("I will keep on traveling West... and find another telescope—and Madge"). "Joshua Cole had fought his first great battle—and won."

**Ch XV Out West.** Gold Belt Cut-off railroad, California; desert town **Spur**; main contractors **Demarest, Spruce and Tillou**. San Antonio Range, 6,000 ft. Hammerman job; Joshua meets **California Bill Fox** (squat, broad-brimmed tan hat, iron-gray hair, black brows, slate-colored eyes, gray flannel shirt; ex-stage driver, ex-deputy sheriff; calls Joshua "Tony"). Bill: Bloodmop died ~3 months earlier; daughter "Shanty Madge" runs outfit with mother; Hill of Springs tunnel; Jawbone (Irish powderman).

**Ch XVI The Road to G-String.** Bill drives six mules. Route: Spur, desert, Wild Woman Springs (saloons: Scotty's, Palace, Gem, Poker Dan's, Midway, Shoestring Charley's, Cowboy Mary's, Forget-me-not), Yucca Flat, Stirrup Lake, Saddle Mountain, Box-R Ranch (owner Lee Sweet). Bill: "Cole of Spyglass Mountain"; "Tony" name; Madge's suitor **Jack Montgomery** (son of Montgomery & Applegate). Bill: "figger it out."

**Ch XVII Ambitions.** Camp One (on lake plateau); Joshua hammerman, crew incl. **Bluenose** (powderman). Madge visits on black gelding; "Hello." Clothes order totaling $17.35 (Stetson $7.50, shoes $5). Madge's mother: "you swept me off my feet... kept me off my feet." Joshua plans cave study; homemade telescope; five-inch telescope ambition; Madge: "Is there any money in it?"

**Ch XVIII New Prospects.** Tunnel tour; Joshua "I came hunting you." Jawbone drinks, overshoots shots. Bill: homestead on Spyglass Mountain (forest reserve; file in LA; $40 loan; "Telescope... Spyglass... Cole of Spyglass Mountain").

**Ch XIX A Trio of Shocks.** John Golden (mining engineer, G-string) runs survey with Joshua; homestead 160 acres at foot of Spyglass Mountain. LA land office; buys brass tubing, lens, tripod. Stage to Ragtown (tent saloons: Silver Dollar, Golden Eagle). Sees Whimperer running skeleton-dance game; chases him into tent of **Slim Wolfgang** (runs stud game in Golden Eagle). Slim: "Fifty-six thirty-five?" Returns to camp: Jawbone fired big shot drunk; tunnel slide; "Shanty Madge ruined."

**Ch XX "A Little Sleep".** Mrs. Mundy: outfit debts; Demarest, Spruce and Tillou to take outfit; Mrs. Mundy wants homestead. Joshua advises filing secretly. Engineers (Emanuel Peters, etc.). Demarest offers $2,500 reward (raised later to $5,000). Joshua says he'll use "horse sense." On his evening walk to Mundys: rifle shot from trees; shot in left shoulder. "All he wanted was a little sleep."

**Ch XXI The Surrender.** Ragtown "hospital" (two-room pine shack); **Dr. J. Miles Stanhope** (Van Dyke beard, drunk, roulette, Gladys). Joshua found by two stiffs. Madge visits, smoothes hair; gives up outfit ("I'm through"). Land office letter: Joshua's claim allowed (160 acres, San Antonio Mountains).

**Ch XXII Hercules and His Firebrand.** Joshua proposes plan: "coyote hole" (sketch A-I) running around slide B, timbering through it; "work behind the pressure." Philip Demarest ("Heavens to Betsy!"; ruddy, white-bearded, bluff). Engineers laugh; Madge rebukes Demarest. Plan works; slide joined. Demarest: $5,000 and job; Joshua refuses. Mars: June 18 next year best since 1909; eight-inch telescope to buy.

**Ch XXIII "When the Moment Comes!"** Mundys' tent; Bill's signs of hard winter (yellowjackets, ground squirrels). Madge: "Is there any money in it?" Joshua's Mars theory: canals, oases, Marconi wireless on yacht *Electra*, Edison, B. McAfee; Lowell Observatory; "a figure... for one brief moment." **Jack Montgomery** enters: "Cole of Spyglass Mountain."

**Ch XXIV Water at Ragtown.** Montgomery (Eastern college, insincere, polite tolerance). Joshua buys $2,000 eight-inch telescope (advertised), saddle, bridle, martingales; buys dapple-gray horse for $500, names it **Argo**. Madge's move: wagons, mules. Ragtown: **Lee Sweet** (huge, half-moon whiskers, drunk, fancy spurs) threatens Joshua; Joshua shoves him; Bill calms him ("cultus").

**Ch XXV On the Rocky Road to Ragtown.** Camp at sienega; sunset on lake. Joshua & Madge alone; "Shanty Madge, I love you." Madge: "I don't know"; Montgomery proposed. O'Reilly poem "A Dreamer Lives Forever." Madge hears horsemen.

**Ch XXVI The Moron.** Bill arrives with **The Whimperer** drunk on his load. Joshua defines "moron" (bromide plus). Bill's Spur supply-depot quarrel; "You—you moron!"

**Ch XXVII "Nuttin' but de Trut'".** Whimperer confesses: stole telescope, sold for $100; Slim hired him to track Joshua from Hathaway; Slim shot Joshua (30-30 rifle borrowed "to hunt deer"); Slim paid by John Cole. Slim's girl Winnie; Lee Sweet's threats. Joshua pays Whimperer $10 + pint flask; he boards stage.

**Ch XXVIII "You'll Come Back to Spyglass Mountain".** **Winnie the Weeper** (Slim's girl) reads Whimperer's letter (demands $25 via Mother Duffy, Oakland bar, Sacramento). Madge in overalls, carpenter's apron. Cabin, stable, observatory; telescope (10-ft tube, iron pedestal, clock drive). Trail to summit; Spyglass ~1,000 ft above lake (lake 6,750 ft). Madge & Joshua speech: "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain!"

**Ch XXIX Winter in the San Antones.** Observatory with revolving dome ("A Home-made Observatory for $300" in *The Universe*, $25). Articles: "Speculations on the Physiology and Anatomy of the Inhabitants of Mars" (*The American Astronomer*, $10); "Fissures or Canals?" and "The Atmosphere of Mars"; "Is Mars a Lifeless Planet?" (*The Journal of Astronomy*, $50); autobiography titled "Cole of Spyglass Mountain." *The Scientist* attacks; *Scientific Weekly* defends. Eratosthenes crater vegetation sighting. Optical experiments. Lester visit planned. Felix Wolfgang "takes a hand."

**Ch XXX Slim Wolfgang Plans.** Slim overheard Joshua say he'd go East late April. Winnie confronts Slim. Slim's account: Peter Henry Florence's will leaves Joshua $150,000 at 21; if Joshua dies, to Lester (birthday June 15). John Cole hires Slim ($5,000 advance, $15,000 then $25,000 offered) to keep Joshua away till 21. Slim trailed Joshua with Whimperer; Whimperer stole telescope; Slim shot Joshua. Plan: Lee Sweet to run Joshua off. Slim: "I won't let Fifty-six thirty-five get dat jack for half."

**Ch XXXI Bullets from Spyglass Mountain.** Madge & mother leave for LA (Mary Montgomery invitation; Jack lives in city apartment). Joshua/Madge ride; Lee Sweet and four vaqueros fire at Joshua's cabin roof from shelf; three then four shots. Madge: "is it possible that you are a coward?" Joshua: "Fiddlesticks"; "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain."

**Ch XXXII The Night of June Fifteenth.** Bill advises Joshua (write Madge). Sweet's men set fire at Joshua's cabin (five buckets saved it). Madge's letter: rejects Joshua ("I am too shallow"; marrying Jack; "Contritely, MADGE"). Bill tracks Slim and Winnie to tent; overhears trunk-packing for Spur; holds Slim; Bill's hidden .32 automatic; Slim's gun taken.

**Ch XXXIII Horsemen in the Night.** Joshua alone on summit observing Mars (June 18 close approach; Mars 42 million miles). Bill arrives with Slim; Slim confesses to Joshua. Joshua tells Bill to free Slim. Bill kicks nothing; lets Slim ride off.

**Ch XXXIV When the Moment Came.** Joshua's mind on Mars; at 12:10 a.m. (alarm clock) sees hairline figure; sets camera; shots from Sweet's men pierce dome; Joshua falls down ladder. Bill telegraphs Dr. Hiram A. Buck, Milton University (Elmfield, Mass.): figure "central to Uranius, Nilokeras, and Ganges"; Buck: not observed elsewhere. Madge returns (Bill fetches her in LA; Montgomerys' apartment). In hospital Joshua near death; Madge: "I've come back to Spyglass Mountain." Telegrams: Ernest G. Pratt (Tabor Univ.), John F. Quincy (Sanborn, Ohio), Harvey G. Mills. Newspaper: Dr. Emanuel Schlott (German telescopist) photographed the figure; "COLE OF SPYGLASS MOUNTAIN FAMOUS IN A NIGHT." Ends with Madge and Joshua together.

## BOOK 2: THE DUKE DECIDES
Author: Headon Hill. A. Wessels Co., 1903 (New York).

**Ch I The Man with the Mandate.** Charles Hanbury, ex-cavalry subaltern (India polo; ruined by extravagance), lamed in hatchway fall, works as adding clerk in NYC dry-goods store ($8/week, pays $5 for boarding-house). Bowery encounter with stout Englishman **Jevons** (Panama hat, Cockney). Saloon: $500 in notes. Job: plant faked US Treasury bonds on Bank of England, £3 million; sail on *St. Paul*; see **Mr. Clinton Ziegler** at Hotel Cecil, London; death threat. Telegram: uncle and cousin killed in railway accident; Hanbury inherits as **7th Duke of Beaumanoir** (family solicitors Pattisons; Morgan's bank).

**Ch II On Board the *St. Paul*.** Beaumanoir books as "Charles Hanbury." **Leonie Sherman** (American, Senator's daughter; mother Mrs. Sherman "spreads herself" for English dukes). Walks; friendship grows. Warning: spy **Marker** (brown covert-coat, tweed cap) watches Beaumanoir.

**Ch III A Task-master in Goggles.** Southampton, Waterloo; Mrs. Sherman invites him to 140 Grosvenor Gardens (Sadgrove house). Hotel Cecil: Ziegler (white beard, purple cheeks, blue glasses, invalid chair, parrot falsetto). Masked men attack; Ziegler spares him: "Let him alone." Ziegler knows Senator Sherman carries the real bonds; Ziegler's agent arranged seating. Deadline: Saturday noon.

**Ch IV The Lady in the Landau.** Forsyth meets Beaumanoir on stairs. Alec Forsyth: Eton friend, Foreign Office clerk (£230 p.a.), now Beaumanoir's secretary (£800). Beaumanoir's cousin **Sybil Hanbury** (18). Forsyth loves Sybil. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton (handsome blonde, childish voice) in landau; invites to tea Saturday at Cecil. Beaumanoir refuses. Decides to stop serving Ziegler.

**Ch V Ziegler Begins to Move.** Prior's Tarrant (Hertfordshire). Forsyth's letter. Church; vicar **Mr. Bristow**. Gardener Jennings lassoed in park. Night: charcoal brazier in chimney; Beaumanoir wakes choking.

**Ch VI The General is Curious.** Tea at 140 Grosvenor Gardens: Mrs. Sadgrove, Mrs. Sherman, Leonie, Sybil. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's bold eyes. **General Jem Sadgrove** (ex-Indian Staff Corps, C.B., Thug/Dacoit hunter, "nose of a fox-terrier"). He saw Eglinton's carriage knock Beaumanoir down. Senator Sherman carrying bonds to London. Beaumanoir warns: "cable him to look out."

**Ch VII The Men on the Stairs.** Forsyth's John Street rooms (Adelphi). Beaumanoir hides there; Marker at door with bogus "Mr. Crofton" errand. Forsyth goes to club, returns: two men (fake clergyman; burly bull-necked in tweeds) descending; door forced; Beaumanoir gone.

**Ch VIII The Cut Panel.** Beaumanoir House, Piccadilly; white drawing-room; butler **Prince**. Fake Scotland Yard "Inspector Chantrey" (clergyman garb) tries to see Beaumanoir. Sybil intervenes. Beaumanoir arrives; Forsyth arrives; all stay the night. 3 a.m.: Sybil hears sawing; catches intruder (tweeds, bowler, revolver). Beaumanoir disarms; escorts intruder out. Watch-spring saw cut panel.

**Ch IX The Strategy of the General.** Sadgrove at Beaumanoir House. Duke refuses police. Sadgrove: go to Prior's Tarrant with house-party (Shermans, Sadgroves, Sybil, Forsyth). Azimoolah Khan summoned. Apple-woman surveillance; Steptoe footman; woman vanishes with man "dressed as clergyman."

**Ch X A Duty Call.** Sadgrove checks Scotland Yard (no "Chantrey"). Calls on Mrs. Talmage Eglinton with ladies. Her suite adjoins Ziegler's (communicating door). Azimoolah stages "Indian Prince" (Thakore of Bhurtnagur) disturbance next door. Sadgrove reveals Duke goes to Prior's Tarrant "by the 8.45 from St. Pancras" with Forsyth (deliberate bait).

**Ch XI On the Terrace.** Sadgrove at Prior's Tarrant; Azimoolah spies painters with fake deer. 8.45 derailed (timber barrier between St. Albans and Harpenden). Forsyth returns to Tarrant Road station; false telegram "Sybil Hanbury, Beaumanoir House." Sadgrove deduces Mrs. Eglinton = Ziegler's partner. Two prowlers on terrace; Sadgrove grabs Azimoolah by mistake: "That's your own man, Azimoolah!"

**Ch XII The Man Under the Seat.** Beaumanoir on train (Kentish Town, Hendon, Mill Hill, Elstree). Finds Marker under seat; questioning; Marker shows ticket; guard. Second tall "toff" in another compartment. Radlett. Obstruction: train stopped on steep gradient (woods). Beaumanoir flees into wood; signal whistles; ends at ride, then to lane.

**Ch XIII At the Keeper's Cottage.** Beaumanoir reaches keeper **Mayne**'s cottage (Sir Claude Asprey's coverts; Beaumanoir shot first pheasant there at Eton age). Mayne: "Providence must have been in two minds." American impostor "Colonel Anstruther Walcot, 14th Dragoon Guards." Beaumanoir escapes via woodshed roof and faggot-pile. Public footpath, sign-post. Azimoolah follows, ambushes at terrace; Duke attacks, Sadgrove intervenes.

**Ch XIV Too Many Women.** Breakfast: Beaumanoir reports Mrs. Eglinton accepts invitation. Sadgrove realizes Sybil in danger. Anonymous note "There is danger from Ziegler," scented like Eglinton's letter. Sadgrove and Sybil talk on terrace: "Too many women in it." Sybil deduces Eglinton's plot.

**Ch XV A New Cure for Headache.** Tapestry-room; Leonie sings; Sybil feeds Mrs. Eglinton fake gossip (Sadgrove to Ziegler). Eglinton "headache." Maid **Rosa** (French). Night: Eglinton exits, Azimoolah follows to park wall; dog-cart with two men toward St. Albans (3.15 night mail). Next morning Eglinton "confined to bed." Ziegler's letter via village post: gentleman "reconsidered"; secretary to call Monday.

**Ch XVI A Delicate Mission.** Sunday: Eglinton asks carriage to station (Forsyth escort; "leases at solicitors"). Forsyth goes to Ziegler's suite; **Leopold Benzon** (Ziegler's secretary, the "Walcot" fake). Ziegler's interview; Forsyth denies knowing plan. Benzon gives sealed letter for Duke. Forsyth meets Eglinton on stairs; she claims going out; Kettner's lunch; Forsyth declares "very far from being indifferent."

**Ch XVII Where is the Duke?** Senator Sherman due. Beaumanoir vanishes (leaves window unlatched; bed slept; cold toilet). Azimoolah reports Duke walked to Tring station; train to Bletchley; North of England express to Liverpool. Mrs. Eglinton tells party all is well.

**Ch XVIII The Senator and the Securities.** Senator Leonidas Sherman on *Campania* at Liverpool; purser Seaton. Duke meets Senator at landing stage; Senator suspects confidence trick. Corridor express; Duke's pistol. Prior's Tarrant; Beaumanoir takes box into fireproof safe in muniment room (green-and-gold patent safe; key kept by Duke).

**Ch XIX In the Crypt.** Sadgrove and Senator discuss "Cora Lestrade" (organizer, escaped jail). Forsyth impersonates Duke (make-up). Ziegler's letter: Duke to unfasten crypt door. Crypt: five figures; Forsyth limps, gives tissue-paper packet. Ziegler discovers swap, begs for return of bogus bonds; Forsyth refuses; sends Ziegler off through garden door.

**Ch XX In the Muniment Room.** Beaumanoir guards safe with revolver. Letter to Ziegler had been written jointly by Sadgrove and Forsyth. Ziegler (actually woman, "Cora Lestrade") with Rosa and Benzon. Benzon and gang enter via window; Beaumanoir switches light, grabs Ziegler. General, Senator, Forsyth, Sybil arrive. Azimoolah chokes gang man. Ziegler's wig removed: Mrs. Talmage Eglinton. Sadgrove explains: Sybil deduced the identity; Forsyth never hurt. Lestrade and Benzon released. Lestrade leaves in morning in high spirits.

**Ch XXI The Honor of the House.** Bonds reach Bank of England; Senator and Duke and Sadgrove return by train. Beaumanoir confesses to Senator; Senator's praise ("a straight man"). Beaumanoir says he'd have accepted the bribe offer but for the Shermans. Six months later: Forsyth married Sybil in September; Beaumanoir married Leonie (Duke and Duchess honeymooning in Egypt). Forsyth reads *Standard* report: Cora Lestrade stabbed on Vienna mail (traveling as "Countess Poniatowski"); arrest of a man dressed as Roman priest. Sybil notes the General's insight came from a woman's knowledge.
